summary: The requested relation itself has t(t-1) rows, giving an Omega(t^2) output lower bound matched by the filtered Cartesian product.

optimality.argument: Every one of t teams must be paired as home with each of the other t-1 teams, so any correct result contains t(t-1) distinct rows. Emitting that output requires quadratic time, and the cross join examines exactly t^2 candidate pairs before removing t self-pairs.

replacement_checks.evidence: The mandated output cardinality is t(t-1), which is quadratic in the number of teams.
The query generates t^2 Cartesian pairs and applies one constant-time inequality test to each.
Authored cases cover two, three, and four teams, both orientations, self-pair exclusion, lexical order, and spaced names.
